claim.pdf_says: BLOCK CONTAINS [integer-1 TO] integer-2 {RECORDS / CHARACTERS} (RECORDS underlined; CHARACTERS printed without underline)
claim.why_it_matters: Same added underline in the report-file FD (V-12): the printed CHARACTERS is not underlined and so is optional (§1985:IV.2.1.2); the markdown makes it a required key word.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered page 204 (V-12, REPORT FILE FD) at 300 dpi. In the BLOCK CONTAINS clause the printed glyphs show BLOCK, TO and RECORDS underlined, while CHARACTERS in the lower slot of the braces has no underline; the underline rules on the other key words on the page (RECORD, TO, LABEL, STANDARD) are clearly visible, so the missing one is not a rendering loss. The transcription at page-204.md line 33 has <u>CHARACTERS</u>. That adds an underline the PDF does not have, so it changes the word's status from optional to key word. The braces on that line have no choice-indicator bars, so under §1985:IV.2.1.4 exactly one of RECORDS/CHARACTERS is selected, explicitly or implicitly. Because CHARACTERS is not underlined, writing 'BLOCK CONTAINS integer-2' with neither word selects CHARACTERS by default. The markdown's underline removes that default. The difference is in content and is normative.
verdict.corrected_description: The PDF prints CHARACTERS in the BLOCK CONTAINS braces of the report-file FD (V-12) without an underline. It is an optional word, so when neither RECORDS nor CHARACTERS is written, CHARACTERS is implicitly selected. The markdown underlines CHARACTERS, which makes it a key word and drops the implicit default. The claim is correct in substance; 'required key word' should read 'key word that must be written explicitly when chosen, which removes the implicit default'.
